isFailsLedgerTrue.question: VF31's standing objection was that 'Nothing was written.' is a structural belief rather than a count of actual writes. Does the ledger count actual writes?
isFailsLedgerTrue.answer: YES. It is true, and it is true for the right reason.
isFailsLedgerTrue.howIVerified: Every write channel in the builder was enumerated: there are exactly three fs.writeFileSync call sites (line 458 inside writeJson, line 1517 for the fixture PDFs, line 1895 for participant-instructions.md) and no appendFileSync, cpSync, renameSync, copyFileSync, createWriteStream, execSync or spawnSync anywhere in the file. Each of the three is followed IMMEDIATELY by noteWritten(rel) — 459, 1518, 1896 — so the ledger is appended after the byte-write returns, per actual write, not per intention. filesWritten is a plain array and fail() branches on its length. I then extracted filesWritten, noteWritten and fail verbatim and drove fail() directly with process.exit bound to a throw: with an empty ledger it prints exactly 'Nothing was written.'; after two noteWritten calls it prints 'Nothing further will be written, but 2 file(s) were already written to disk before this refusal and are still there. They are the partial output of a run that then refused, they are not a packet, and they are not to be read as one:' followed by each path and the note that each is rewritten from the pinned source bytes on the next successful run.
isFailsLedgerTrue.andTheReorderingClaimIsExact: VERIFIED against the parent builder at 12d01df56. OLD: the four fixture PDFs (line 1279) and eight writeJson reports (1315, 1352, 1377, 1419, 1433, 1480, 1495, 1556) all precede the checks at 1572-1574 — TWELVE files. NEW: only the four fixture writes (1517) precede petitionPageFacts/fingerprint/prefills at 1568-1570 and the two new guards at 1580/1582 — FOUR files, and they are the fixtures. 'Twelve used to, four do now' is exactly right.
isFailsLedgerTrue.oneImprecisionWorthRecording: FIX01 writes that the checks 'read the finished fixtures, so they cannot run before the four fixture PDFs.' Slightly overstated. The refusal set that drives the guards comes from fx.report.written, which is the in-memory finalizer report, not the bytes on disk. What genuinely requires the disk write is verifyFromBytes(), which is handed a PATH and calls flattenedWidgets(file). So the four writes are required by the CURRENT code path but not by the guards themselves; a later lane could pass bytes instead and move all four below the guards too. This does not weaken the repair — it means the remaining four are reducible rather than irreducible.
isFailsLedgerTrue.residualWindow: noteWritten is called after writeFileSync returns. If a write threw mid-file, a partial file would exist unnamed — but that path throws uncaught and never reaches fail(), so the ledger is never wrong about a refusal it actually prints.

thingsFoundHereThatNoCounterCanSee: STEP 4 IS THE ONE PLACE THE REPAIR'S OWN STANDARD IS NOT APPLIED EVENLY, AND IT IS THE PETITION'S. Step 10 opens conditionally for the order — 'each written only where it fits the order's own rule and left empty where it does not'. Step 4 opens with a flat assertion for the petition — 'The caption above the title is already filled in — check it, and complete by hand any blank that arrived empty.' The condition is present, so the guard passes it and it is not an undisclosed refusal, but the leading clause is what a participant working a numbered checklist reads, and on the boundary case it is maximally false: zero of that caption's five blanks are filled.

AND THE CONDITION STEP 4 OFFERS IS THE WRONG EXPLANATION FOR TWO OF THE FIVE. Each caption has FIVE blanks — IN THE, COURT OF, DIVISION, Case No, First/Middle/Last name — and production-field-map.json shows decision=refuse for IN THE and DIVISION on BOTH documents: the packet never attempts them. Step 4's only offered reason for an empty caption blank is that a value 'arrived empty', i.e. was too long for its rule. The packet recovers this in step 5, in the county paragraph, in 'The court's name in both captions' and in table rows 1 and 2, so no participant is left without the answer; but step 4 taken alone mis-explains why two of the five blanks are blank.

THE CONSISTENCY GUARD STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SEE THAT. Its anchors are built only from [...new Set(refusable.map((r) => r.field))] — the measured REFUSAL set.
